old: Its root sense had nothing to do with money — it meant simply the custom or use of a thing.
It first named someone who knew the usages of trade, a kind of go-between for deals.
It shares a Germanic root with the verb brook, in its old meaning 'to use or tolerate.'
clues: This name for a kind of business professional traces back to an ancient root meaning 'to use, enjoy,' and in medieval times simply meant a small trader.
A go-between who arranges deals in stocks, insurance or property for clients, earning a commission. Unlike a dealer, they don't buy and sell on their own account.
Behind-the-scenes political kingmakers are called 'power' ones, and diplomats are said to do this as a verb when they negotiate a truce or peace deal.
